items.item: Sources/SwiftUI Extensions/Sequence+PDF.swift — a block taller than the page area is sil
items.reason: Platform I can't check: every source and test file is inside #if canImport(SwiftUI) and uses ImageRenderer/CGContext/PDFKit, so nothing here compiles or runs on Linux. The options also need an owner choice: rejecting needs a typed throw (API change: pdf(...) returns Data today), a precondition would trap on caller input (forbidden), and splitting means rendering one block across several pages by offsetting and clipping it (render the block once per page slice with .offset(y: -k*height) inside a page-height clipped frame), which has to be verified on macOS with PDFKit.

Owner decision plus platform: reading a real fold needs an Apple API that can't be checked here, and renaming the public modifier is an API break across apps (no uses found in repos/, but the Mac apps are outside this checkout). The README already states that without simulation it provides no division.

items.item: Sources/SwiftUI Extensions/Markdown.swift — unordered list items get numbers and every h
items.reason: Platform I can't check: Markdown is SwiftUI/AttributedString-only and its blocks are private, so neither the change nor its test can be compiled here. Proposed change: in Markdown.Block take the innermost list kind from `kinds` (first .orderedList/.unorderedList) and pass Numbered a bullet for unordered items (Numbered appends '.', so it needs a label-without-dot initializer or a separate Bulleted view); map header levels 1/2/3/4+ to .title/.title2/.title3/.headline; make Block internal and test the classification and the plain-text fallback with @testable import on macOS.

notes: No changes made and no worktree created: the whole package is Apple-only (SwiftUI, PDFKit), and per the brief items that need a platform I can't check stay open. These are best done in a session on the Mac, where ci.yml's macOS job and swift test can verify them.
